note: DEMO FIXTURE — modern-English paraphrases of attested traditional claims, not verbatim spans.

passages.title: The Complete Herbal
passages.author: Nicholas Culpeper
passages.text: Lavender is of a sharp and keen scent, and is reported to comfort the brain and the nerves, and to be good against the falling sickness, the palsy, and the trembling of the joints. The flowers steeped in wine are given for the head and the spirits.

passages.title: The Complete Herbal
passages.author: Nicholas Culpeper
passages.text: Lungwort is so called because the leaves are spotted like the lungs of a man, and therefore it was held by the signature of the thing to be a sovereign remedy for all diseases of the lungs, for coughs, and for the shortness of breath.

passages.title: The Complete Herbal
passages.author: Nicholas Culpeper
passages.text: Wormwood is bitter and warming; it strengthens the stomach, kills worms, and is good for a weak digestion. The juice of the herb is used outwardly, and the decoction inwardly.

passages.title: The Complete Herbal
passages.author: Nicholas Culpeper
passages.text: Liquorice root is hot and moist in quality; it is good for the roughness of the throat, the hoarseness of the voice, and the sharpness of humours, and it is often boiled in waters for the breast.

passages.title: The Herball or Generall Historie of Plantes
passages.author: John Gerard
passages.text: The distilled water of Lavender drawn in a bath of warm water, that the fire touch it not, is of all the waters the most comfortable to the head and to the sinews; and being smelled unto it refresheth the spirits.

passages.title: The Herball or Generall Historie of Plantes
passages.author: John Gerard
passages.text: Rosemary is a remedy against the stuffings of the head, and the water thereof distilled is used to wash the temples; the herb is accounted to strengthen the memory.

passages.title: On the Nature of Things (spagyric writings)
passages.author: Paracelsus
passages.text: The spagyric artist separates the three principles from the plant: the sulphur, which is the oil and the scent; the mercury, which is the spirit and the water; and the salt, which remaineth in the ashes. Each is prepared apart, and then joined again, that the virtue may be more open.

passages.title: The Compound of Alchymy (Ripley Scroll tradition)
passages.author: George Ripley
passages.text: Calcine the body until it be white and friable, then dissolve it in a moist menstruum, and digest it in gentle heat for a season, closing the vessel that nothing evaporate.

passages.title: The Compound of Alchymy (Ripley Scroll tradition)
passages.author: George Ripley
passages.text: Putrefaction is the first gate: the matter must be dissolved into blackness and be suffered to rest in the dung of a horse, or in a bath of temperate heat, until the colour change.

passages.title: Rosarium Philosophorum
passages.author: anon. (Pseudo-Arnaldus)
passages.text: In the bath of Mary the vessel is warmed with the heat of water only, so that the gentle heat may draw the spirit without burning it; this is the distillation that admitteth no violence.

passages.title: De Simplicium Medicamentorum Facultatibus
passages.author: Galen of Pergamon
passages.text: The faculties of simples are taken from their qualities; the hot and dry herb attenuates, the cold and moist herb thickens, and the physician must temper the one with the other, considering the heat of the body and the season of the year.

passages.title: De Materia Medica
passages.author: Pedanius Dioscorides
passages.text: Peony: the root dried and drunk helpeth the falling sickness, and the seed taken in wine appeaseth the pains of the belly. The root of the female peony is of the greater virtue.

passages.title: Bencao Gangmu (Compendium of Materia Medica, trans.)
passages.author: Li Shizhen
passages.text: Dang gui: the root nourishes the blood and moves it, quiets the spirit, and is used when the menses are irregular or when the blood is deficient and the face is pale. It is warmed with wine.

passages.title: Bencao Gangmu (Compendium of Materia Medica, trans.)
passages.author: Li Shizhen
passages.text: Dan shen: the root invigorates the blood, cools the heart, and quiets the spirit; it is given when the blood is stasis and the chest is oppressed. It is decocted in water or in wine.

passages.title: Charaka Samhita (English trans.)
passages.author: Agnivesha / Charaka
passages.text: The physician should consider the country, the season, the digestive fire of the patient, the strength of the body and the nature of the illness, for the same drug acts differently in different constitutions.

passages.title: King's American Dispensatory
passages.author: Harvey W. Felter & John U. Lloyd
passages.text: Liquorice is demulcent and expectorant, and is largely employed to mask the taste of nauseous medicines; in large doses, long continued, it has been known to produce puffiness of the face and swelling of the ankles, and to disorder the action of the heart.

passages.title: King's American Dispensatory
passages.author: Harvey W. Felter & John U. Lloyd
passages.text: Peony is antispasmodic and tonic; it has been recommended in chorea, in spasms of the muscles, and in the convulsive affections of childhood.

passages.title: A Modern Herbal
passages.author: Maud Grieve
passages.text: Lavender. The volatile oil is obtained by distilling the fresh flowering tops with water. It is used in nervous affections, in giddiness and sick headache, and as a stimulant in faintness.

passages.title: A Modern Herbal
passages.author: Maud Grieve
passages.text: Horehound. The herb is esteemed for its bitter tonic action and for coughs; it gently promotes expectoration. Its bitterness is very great, and it is given as a syrup or an infusion.

passages.title: Paradisi in Sole Paradisus Terrestris
passages.author: John Parkinson
passages.text: The leaves of Sage are hot and dry, and are held to quicken the memory and to restore the senses, and the decoction thereof gargled helpeth the mouth and the throat.

passages.title: Huangdi Neijing — Suwen (trans.)
passages.author: anon. (Yellow Emperor corpus)
passages.text: The channels of the body carry the qi and the blood; where the qi is blocked there is pain, and where the blood is stasis the pain is fixed and pricking. Needling is applied where the channel is obstructed.

passages.title: Zhenjiu Jiayi Jing (Systematic Classic of Acupuncture, trans.)
passages.author: Huangfu Mi
passages.text: The point Zusanli is on the leg below the knee; needling it regulates the stomach and the spleen and is used when the digestion is weak and the limbs are cold.

passages.title: EMA herbal monographs (selected)
passages.author: European Medicines Agency
passages.text: Lavender flower: traditional herbal medicinal product for the relief of mild symptoms of mental stress and exhaustion, and for the relief of mild sleep disorders, on the basis of longstanding use.

passages.title: EMA herbal monographs (selected)
passages.author: European Medicines Agency
passages.text: Liquorice root: contraindicated in patients with hypertension, hypokalaemia, or a history of fluid retention; use is limited to a maximum of four to six weeks because of the mineralocorticoid effect.

passages.title: EMA herbal monographs (selected)
passages.author: European Medicines Agency
passages.text: Peony root: traditional use for the relief of mild spasms and cramping in the lower abdomen; combinations with liquorice root are traditional in Japanese kampo medicine for muscle cramp.

passages.title: Dr Duke's Phytochemical and Ethnobotanical Databases
passages.author: James A. Duke (USDA ARS)
passages.text: Lavandula angustifolia: linalool, linalyl acetate, borneol, camphor, terpinen-4-ol. Reported activity records for the volatile oil include sedative, anxiolytic and antimicrobial.

passages.title: Dr Duke's Phytochemical and Ethnobotanical Databases
passages.author: James A. Duke (USDA ARS)
passages.text: Marrubium vulgare: marrubiin, premarrubiin, marrubenol. Reported activity records include bitter stimulant, expectorant and antispasmodic.

passages.title: ChEMBL — compound bioactivity records (subset)
passages.author: EMBL-EBI
passages.text: Bioactivity records: linalool and linalyl acetate screened against GABA receptor complexes; flumazenil-reversible modulation of the benzodiazepine site reported in the patch-clamp literature summary table.

passages.title: World Flora Online / WCVP taxonomy backbone
passages.author: WFO Consortium
passages.text: Lavandula angustifolia Mill. — accepted name in the WCVP backbone; family Lamiaceae. Former usage 'Lavandula vera' is listed as a synonym.

passages.title: World Flora Online / WCVP taxonomy backbone
passages.author: WFO Consortium
passages.text: Marrubium vulgare L. — accepted; family Lamiaceae; syn. Marrubium apulum. Peucedanum ostruthium is listed under Apiaceae.

passages.title: Huangdi Neijing — Suwen (trans.)
passages.author: anon. (Yellow Emperor corpus)
passages.text: The five viscera are each associated with a colour, a season, an emotion and a taste; the physician who reads the complexion and the pulse may know the state of the viscera without asking the patient.
